description: openPaneInSession splits an explicit pane (the orchestrator) with an explicit size, so the worker-pane geometry is deterministic in create and recreate regardless of which pane is active.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: split-window accepts `-t target-pane` to target an explicit pane and `-l size` where size may be followed by '%' for a percentage of available space; `-v` is a vertical split (default). resize-pane `-x`/`-y` accept a column/row count or a '%' suffix. Confirms `split-window -t <orchPaneId> -v -l <size>` is the canonical deterministic form; note CAM-48: resize-pane -x rejects #{...} format expressions, so use literal numbers/percent only.

userStories.title: Target the orchestrator pane with an explicit size in openPaneInSession
userStories.description: As a cam operator, I need the worker-pane to be born from a fixed pane (the orchestrator) at a fixed size so that it never inherits a tiny 49x24 geometry from whatever pane (e.g. the dashboard column) happened to be active during a recreate.
acceptanceCriteria: openPaneInSession accepts an explicit target pane id parameter and issues `tmux split-window -t <targetPaneId> ...` (the literal pane id, e.g. %0), NOT the bare window target `<session>:0`. [oracle: file-assert grep -n "'-t'" /Users/eduardo/Documents/Projects/cam-cli/src/tmux/session.ts shows the split-window arg sourced from the new pane-id parameter, and grep -q -- '${sessionName}:0' on the split-window argv inside openPaneInSession returns no match]

The split-window argv includes an explicit size flag `-l <size>` (vertical split, so size is rows or a percentage) giving the worker the prominent/readable share; the chosen value is documented in this story's notes. [oracle: file-assert grep -nE "'-l'" /Users/eduardo/Documents/Projects/cam-cli/src/tmux/session.ts within openPaneInSession]

The single production caller (src/supervisor/host.ts ensureWorkerPaneFn ~366-383) resolves the orchestrator pane id (via getOrchPaneId(sessionName, spawnFn), already imported) and threads it into openPaneInSession, with a deterministic fallback when getOrchPaneId returns null. [oracle: file-assert grep -n 'getOrchPaneId' /Users/eduardo/Documents/Projects/cam-cli/src/supervisor/host.ts shows the resolved id passed to openPaneInSession]

The argv-shape unit test in test/tmux-session.test.ts asserts the split-window argv contains `-t <explicit-pane-id>` (a %<n>-style id, not `<session>:0`) and the `-l` size flag. [oracle: bun test test/tmux-session.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint passes (bun run lint). [oracle: bun run lint]
userStories.notes: Files: src/tmux/session.ts (openPaneInSession ~431-450 — add an explicit targetPaneId parameter and an `-l` size flag to the split-window argv; update the JSDoc ~411-430 which still says `-t <sessionName>:0` and no size); src/supervisor/host.ts (ensureWorkerPaneFn ~366-383 — the ONLY production caller; resolve getOrchPaneId(sessionName, ...) and thread it; pick a deterministic fallback target when it returns null, e.g. the existing currentId/workerPaneId or `${sessionName}:0` — keep behavior safe when the orch pane is gone); test/tmux-session.test.ts (openPaneInSession describe block ~343-410 — update the existing `-t cam-orch-...:0` assertions to the new explicit-pane-id contract and add the `-l` assertion); test/integration/ensure-worker-pane-selfheal.test.ts (~117 also calls openPaneInSession — update its arity to match the new signature so it still compiles/runs). GEOMETRY DECISION: split the orchestrator pane vertically (`-v`) and give the WORKER the larger/readable share. With a 50-row session the orchestrator pane is ~49 rows; `split-window -v -l 60%` makes the new (worker) pane the larger lower share. Prefer a percentage (`-l 60%`) over absolute rows so it scales with terminal height; document the exact number you pick. tmux 3.6a: `-l` accepts a trailing `%` (confirmed in officialDocsConsulted); the sibling split in ensureProjectSession (session.ts ~359-369) already uses `-h -l String(clampDashboardWidth(220))` as the precedent for an explicit-size split. GOTCHA (CAM-48, in memory): resize-pane -x rejects `#{...}` format expressions — if you normalize post-create with resize-pane, pass only literal numbers/percent, never a tmux format string. GOTCHA (memory: 'fakes mentem' / tmux-introspect): this story's argv-shape test is necessary but NOT sufficient — it cannot prove real tmux geometry; US-002 is the discriminating real-tmux oracle. Skill: none beyond the project gate. Re-check scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md for the `bun run check:all` quality spine before declaring done.

userStories.title: Real-tmux integration test proving deterministic worker-pane geometry on recreate
userStories.description: As a cam maintainer, I need a real-tmux test that recreates the worker-pane while a NON-orchestrator pane is active and asserts the worker is born from the orchestrator pane at the canonical size, so that the CAM-80 fix has a discriminating oracle that fails against pre-fix behavior (a fake-spawn argv test cannot catch tmux geometry).
acceptanceCriteria: A new OS-gated real-tmux integration test (under test/integration/, mirroring test/integration/tmux-introspect.test.ts: private `tmux -L` socket, swapSocketSpawn, test.skipIf(!tmuxAvailable), kill-server teardown) creates a real session, makes a NON-orchestrator pane (the dashboard/right column) the ACTIVE pane via select-pane, then opens the worker-pane through the production openPaneInSession path. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'select-pane' on the new test file AND grep -q 'skipIf' on it]

The test asserts the worker pane's geometry is canonical: its parent split is the orchestrator pane and its size/position matches the chosen prominent geometry from US-001, NOT a small pane born from the active dashboard column (e.g. assert the worker pane width equals the orchestrator pane width / spans the orchestrator column, and its height is the chosen share — measured via real `display-message -p` on #{pane_width}/#{pane_height}/#{pane_left}/#{pane_top}). [oracle: bun test test/integration/<new-worker-pane-geometry>.test.ts]

The assertion is discriminating: it fails against the pre-fix openPaneInSession (bare `<session>:0`, no size) and passes against the US-001 implementation. [oracle: reviewer-judgment — reviewer confirms the asserted geometry could only hold with an explicit orchestrator-pane target + size, e.g. worker width != the narrow active dashboard width]

The new test runs on a private socket (e.g. `cam-it-worker-geo`), never `-L cam`, and tears the server down in afterEach. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'kill-server' on the new test file AND grep -vq "'-L', 'cam'" raw-socket setup confirms the private socket name]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint passes (bun run lint). [oracle: bun run lint]
Tests pass, and the new real-tmux test executes (not skipped) on this machine where tmux 3.6a is present. [oracle: bun test test/integration/<new-worker-pane-geometry>.test.ts]
userStories.notes: Files: test/integration/<new>.test.ts (new file; copy the harness scaffold from test/integration/tmux-introspect.test.ts:31-69 — tmuxRaw on the private socket, swapSocketSpawn that rewrites `-L cam`->the test socket, beforeEach new-session -x 220 -y 50, afterEach kill-server). Drive the worker creation through src/tmux/session.ts openPaneInSession (the real production helper) so the test exercises shipped code, not a reimplementation. SETUP to reproduce the bug premise: create the 2-pane layout (orchestrator pane + a right dashboard column via split-window -h), label/identify the orchestrator pane id, then `select-pane -t <dashboardPaneId>` so the DASHBOARD is active (this is the recreate scenario CAM-65 makes universal). Then call openPaneInSession targeting the orchestrator pane id. MEASUREMENT: use `display-message -p -t <workerPaneId> '#{pane_width};#{pane_height};#{pane_left};#{pane_top}'` (semicolon separator, NOT tab — tmux mangles TAB to `_` in -F/format output per CAM-55 memory). The discriminating assertion: worker pane width spans the orchestrator column (wide), not the ~49-col dashboard column; pre-fix it would be born ~49x24 in the bottom-right. Allow a small tolerance (border rows). GOTCHA (memory tmux-introspect / 'fakes mentem'): this is THE gate — a pure argv-shape fake cannot detect geometry; only this real-tmux round-trip can. GOTCHA: add small Bun.sleepSync(100-200) after each tmux mutation as the sibling integration tests do (tmux applies layout async). Re-check scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md for the OS-gate convention (test.skipIf when tmux absent so CI without tmux still passes) and the `bun run check:all` spine.
